perplexity.description:
Soft Metal: It Ain't Heavy... is a compilation album released in 1988 by Stylus Music, featuring 18 tracks of arena and glam rock material. The collection brings together prominent acts from the heavy metal and hard rock scenes, including Ozzy Osbourne, Whitesnake, and Poison, among others. As a curated compilation rather than a studio album by a single artist, it represents the label's effort to package commercially successful rock tracks under a thematic umbrella during the late 1980s.

The album exemplifies the "soft metal" subgenre—a term applied to melodic hard rock and heavy metal acts that prioritized accessibility and radio-friendly production over the heavier, more aggressive sounds dominating underground metal scenes at the time. The compilation's title carries a playful irony, suggesting that despite the "metal" designation, the included tracks lean toward polished production and mainstream appeal rather than raw intensity.

Soft Metal: It Ain't Heavy... was part of a series released by Stylus Music, with subsequent volumes following in subsequent years. While specific critical reception details are limited, the compilation's existence and continuation as a series suggest it found an audience among listeners seeking established rock acts in an accessible format. The album captures a particular moment in 1980s rock when the distinction between hard rock and heavy metal had become increasingly blurred by commercial considerations and production values.
